subject.title: voice-call: media-stream WebSocket accepts unauthenticated start frames for non-Twilio providers (plivo, telnyx)

question: Should `/voice/stream` fail closed for every non-Twilio provider until provider-owned stream-token validation exists, or should maintainers first add non-Twilio media-stream credentials?
rationale: This changes a WebSocket authentication boundary and may intentionally stop permissive non-Twilio media-stream starts, so owner intent is needed before choosing the permanent security and compatibility shape.

options.title: Fail closed now
options.body: Reject non-Twilio `/voice/stream` starts unless a provider-specific verifier accepts the token, then add regression tests for Twilio success and non-Twilio rejection.

options.title: Add provider tokens first
options.body: Implement provider-owned stream-token issuance and validation for any supported non-Twilio media-stream path before allowing those starts.

options.title: Scope media-stream to Twilio
options.body: Document and enforce that `streaming.enabled` media-stream support is Twilio-only while Telnyx remains on the authenticated realtime stream path.

recommendation.title: Fail closed now
recommendation.body: Reject non-Twilio `/voice/stream` starts unless a provider-specific verifier accepts the token, then add regression tests for Twilio success and non-Twilio rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent history shows the broadest ownership signal for voice-call webhook and media-stream security hardening.
